findings.observation: CLI installs existing createCliRpcFetch globally before loading SDK; selected exact origin/path receives x-aztec-api-key and redirect:error. Credentials omit plus referrer no-referrer returns original fetch without injection. Passing aztecApiKey in config does not by itself add SDK transport auth.

Maintained deployment flow constructs a.createAztecNodeClient(config.aztecNodeUrl), performs actual preflight, and supplies that node to createPXE. It does not select createTrustedPrivateNode. Existing wrapper exported by shared/sdk-entry uses shared/aztec-node-client and limits official client maxBatchSize to3.

Official defaultFetch sends content-type plus extraHeaders, credentials from config, and no no-referrer flag. Under unchanged CLI global wrapper this path should receive the key at exact endpoint (source inference); makeFetch uses retry backoffs from SDK createAztecNodeClient. Full request behavior is not qualified from this source inference.

Trust facade has custom bounded silent no-retry/no-redirect privateFetch with credentials:omit and referrerPolicy:no-referrer; API accepts no capability/transport option. It therefore bypasses the CLI injector and will be rejected by authenticated gateway absent an explicit separately reviewed credential transport. This fail-closed result must not be changed by removing the credential-free bypass globally.
